header.title: PGM XX: Spell against headache, the spell of the Syrian women of Gadara for any inflammation, the spell of the Thessalian Philinna against headache (…: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Papyri Graecae Magicae
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:magic:dclp:65576:grc, from papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (CC BY 3.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY 4.0: credit papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (the source's own licence is CC BY 3.0) and this AI translation.

notes.2.19: Fragmentary: the opening and the end (2.36–37) are mostly lost. ‘hea-’ (2.30) is an unfinished ‘head’, apparently abandoned. In 2.23 the subject of ‘was burned’ is lost, and ‘receiver of mysteries’ (μυστοδόκος) is uncertain in sense.

nodes.text: [...] of the Syrian woman of Gadara:
and on the [highest] mountain it was burned,
seven springs of wolves, seven of [bears],
seven of lions, and seven maidens
Flee, pain of the head, and [...] flees
